thread:
elena: Quick RFC follow-up on streaming reframe options. Problem: many clients expect framed `data: <chunk>` SSE-style frames (old), while our v2 outputs NDJSON objects over a single stream. We need a compatibility strategy that doesn't blow CPU on the hot path. Thoughts?

rishi: My 2c: avoid doing full reserialization at the gateway for high-QPS tenants. Gateway CPU is precious. Options: lightweight proxy that rewrites byte-for-byte when possible (fast path), or push an adapter lib to customers.

tom: Agree. Also consider hybrid: we implement a small edge transform service that runs on separate nodes (scales independently), and the gateway routes flagged tenants there. Keeps gateway lightweight.

elena: I like edge transform nodes. How do we handle backpressure and client disconnects? Rewriting streams often needs buffering which can interact poorly with long-lived responses.

clara: Implementation detail: if v2 sends JSONL like `{"token":"hello"}\n`, v1 expects framed frames like `hello` (example). We can do streaming translation with minimal buffering if we stream-transform as bytes come in and flush per JSON object. Memory usage still grows with max token chunk size. We should set a soft limit per-stream.

jenn a: +1 on soft limits. Also, for Dedicated/private customers, we can offer a deployable sidecar adapter so they never hit our edge transform. That reduces our ops burden and aligns with their compliance needs.

rishi: Telemetry: we must capture metric sets per-tenant for the migration cohort: original_chunk_count, rewritten_chunk_count, extra_latency_ms, cpu_ns_per_request, error_rate_post_rewrite. This will help decide if edge transform is acceptable per tenant.

elena: For rollout, propose: 1) 72h shadow run (no rewrite) collecting diffs, 2) deploy edge-transform nodes in canary, route 1% tenants through transform, 3) monitor for 48h, then increase to 10/33/100 cohorts. Each tenant has a kill-switch.

ops-bot: scheduled: edge-transform canary at 1769991200. Emitting metric `stream_transform.rewrites_total`.

clara: We should also add an explicit request header for client-driven fallback: `X-Rw-Stream-Fallback: v1` so clients that detect a regression can opt-in to rewrites without feature flags. Example: `curl -H "X-Rw-Stream-Fallback: v1" https://api.redwood.ai/v2/stream`

tom: On testing: capture a small corpus of 50 representative prompts per tenant cohort and run end-to-end quality checks (token alignment + human spot checks for hallucination changes). If quality delta > 0.4% we abort and rollback that tenant.

rishi: Cost accounting: edge-transform nodes should be billed to migration project until final cutover; propose tagging with billing code `compat/stream-refactor` so finance can track.

elena: Security note: transformations must preserve no-sensitive-data policies. Don't log raw tokens. Use hashed request ids for correlation.

jenn a: I'll own the sidecar container image and docs for Dedicated/private customers. Will push alpha by EOW.

clara: Perf experiment volunteers: I'll run a microbenchmark comparing (A) gateway inline rewrite, (B) edge-transform node, (C) client adapter (JS). Expected: C fastest per-request, B good ops separation, A worst for CPU. I'll post numbers.

elena: Action items: 1) rishi - telemetry and billing tag, 2) ops - provision edge-transform canary and dashboard, 3) jenna - sidecar alpha, 4) clara - perf numbers + memory limits, 5) elena - update RFC with plan + rollback gates. Schedule 30m sync after canary.

elena: tagging this as follow-up to the streaming compatibility RFC. Thanks all.
